about: Which recordings in data/ are used for what (data/ is not in git). core: replayed by every node tools/check.mjs; library: kept for a reason, replayed with --library; a file in data/ not listed here is unsorted and not used. Numbers per recording: node tools/profile.mjs <name>. Cases: one train, a short window, one rule (node tools/cases.mjs). The core is chosen on the profile and replay numbers, with the reason written here.

slots.coveredBy: saturday daytime (same profile, harder replay); the midday recording is in the library

recordings.name: 2026-11-12T06-00-00-005Z
recordings.why: The busiest traffic recorded: 363 trains at once (most 389), 1,820 real stops, 155 silences of 5 min or more, 54 jumps. Also the page tests' fixed moment (tools/ui-check.mjs).

recordings.name: 2026-11-12T17-01-59-418Z
recordings.why: Evening rush with the most lateness recorded (19 % of trains 6 min or more late, 90 % of passings within 8 min) and the trains Max saw that evening (cases). Chosen over 15-30-00 (16:30, a little busier, less late): the morning already covers the busiest traffic.

recordings.name: 2026-11-11T21-45-41-004Z
recordings.why: Quiet traffic (156 trains at once), the highest share of time in silences (42 %) and of trains without a speed (37 %): silent trains moved by the timetable.

recordings.name: 2026-11-12T23-02-56-574Z
recordings.why: Night: unlike every other recording. 78 trains at once, 62 % never send a speed (mostly freight), 59 % of train time in GPS silences of 30 s or more, 22 % of trains 6 min or more late. Also the first hour with the recorder fix: no stream break.

recordings.name: 2026-11-14T09-00-00-018Z
recordings.why: Saturday daytime: 241 trains at once (most 256), 56 % never send a speed, 52 % of train time in GPS silences of 30 s or more, little lateness (8 % of trains 6 min or more late). The profile is almost the weekday midday's, but the replay is harder: stops driven through 18.6 % (the worst of all recordings; midday 15.9 %, others 11-15 %) and 90 % within 10.3 s (midday 9.4 s). So it takes the midday's place in the core, keeping the check at 5 recordings. Fourth live hour with the recorder fix: no stream break.

recordings.name: 2026-11-13T10-30-00-013Z
recordings.why: Weekday midday: 273 trains at once (most 302), and unlike the rush hours 57 % of trains never send a speed (rush hours 33 %) and 52 % of train time is in GPS silences of 30 s or more (rush hours 40-41 %): many trains moving on silence and the timetable at normal traffic. Lateness low (11 % of trains 6 min or more late). Third live hour with the recorder fix: no stream break. Moved to the library 2026-11-14: Saturday daytime has the same profile and a harder replay, and took its core place.

recordings.name: 2026-11-13T04-00-00-000Z
recordings.why: First trains: the day starting up, 84 trains at once at 05:00 rising to 244 (median 179); 31 % never send a speed, 34 % of train time in GPS silences of 30 s or more, little lateness (6 % of trains 6 min or more late). Library, not core: the night already holds the quiet hours and the morning rush has more trains starting and ending (601 in all against 363 at once). Second live hour with the recorder fix: no stream break.

recordings.name: 2026-11-12T15-30-00-006Z
recordings.why: The busiest evening hour (369 trains at once, 66 jumps); a second rush hour to confirm a change on.

recordings.name: 2026-11-12T19-42-00-050Z
recordings.why: Recorded after Max saw 2567 drive through Stockholms södra (20:38, just before it started); commuter trains through Sst.

recordings.name: 2026-11-11T16-46-20-921Z
recordings.why: The first measurements in the docs (data.md) were made on it; positions only, no timetable, so no planned routes.

cases.seen: Max, live, 2026-11-12 18:34: stopped east of Gnesta while the real train ran ~150 km/h, then raced to catch up (~700 km/h). Cause: tiny track pieces at Södermalm cut the way to Stockholm C, so it couldn't move by the timetable.

Max, live, 2026-11-12 20:38: 2567 drove through Stockholms södra without stopping (not recorded); 2556 at 18:22 is the same pattern, recorded: the real train stood ~40 s (hindsight track; its GPS repeated the platform position 18:21:56-18:23:08).
cases.fixedBy: trains: stand at the planned stops they reach (fix/dwell-at-stops; drawn 0 -> 7 s), and a standing target is braked into, not crept up to (fix/arrive-braking; 7 -> 31 s)

cases.seen: Found in the replay (U-turn hunt, 2026-11-12): GPS wobble at the standing train turned the track ahead round; the drawn train slid ~110 m back and forth at Kallhäll, 18:05.
cases.fixedBy: trains: a direction needs 20 m of movement (main, 'fix/wrong-way')
